reason: The passage presents Joseph's administration as a functioning governmental system that directly benefits the Egyptian people. The narrative demonstrates: (1) wise foresight and planning during the years of plenty, (2) systematic collection and storage of grain, (3) distribution of food to the people during the famine (וַיִּפְתַּח יוֹסֵף אֶֽת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּהֶם וַיִּשְׁבֹּ֣ר לְמִצְרַ֔יִם - 'Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to Egypt'), and (4) the positive outcome of preventing starvation. When Pharaoh directs the hungry people to Joseph (לְכ֣וּ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֔ף), the government provides sustenance. The text portrays this administrative competence and public benefit as exemplary and praiseworthy.
